notes.meaning: David organized the Levite gatekeepers into regular working divisions. The list begins with Meshelemiah from the Korahite clan, descended from Asaph (also known as Ebiasaph). These gatekeepers acted as security guards to keep the sacred courts safe and guide worshippers properly.

Seven sons of Meshelemiah are listed in order of birth, starting with Zechariah. These sons took leading roles alongside their father in protecting the sanctuary gates. God gave this family an honorable place of service in his house.

Obed-edom is introduced with eight sons because God richly blessed him. This blessing grew out of his faithful care for the ark of the covenant when it stayed in his house years before. God often rewards devotion to his presence by building up a family for holy service.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars think this gatekeeper Obed-edom may have been a different person from the man who welcomed the ark into his home.

notes.meaning: Shemaiah, the oldest son of Obed-edom, had sons who became family leaders because they were strong and capable men. The gatekeepers needed physical power and courage to open heavy doors, guard against robbers, and keep order in the courts. God gives his servants the exact strength they need for the tasks he assigns them.

A total of sixty-two men from Obed-edom's family were qualified to serve as temple guards. Every one of them was known for strength and readiness to do this heavy work. Faithfulness in one generation can open doors of active service for children and grandchildren.

Meshelemiah also had eighteen sons and relatives who were strong and capable for the work. Together with Obed-edom's family, they formed the main body of Korahite gatekeepers. Each skilled worker helped ensure that worshippers could enter the sanctuary in safety.

Hosah from the Merari clan had thirteen sons and relatives in this service. His son Shimri was placed first as leader, even though he was not the firstborn, likely because the older line had died out or Shimri was best fitted for the post. God looks for character and ability when giving people responsibility in his work.

These chief men led the divisions of gatekeepers as they took turns serving in the house of the Lord. Their practical duties of guarding and opening the doors were counted just as sacred as the duties of the musicians and priests. Every role in God's service has real dignity in his sight.

The gatekeepers cast lots to assign families to each gate, treating young and old without favoritism. Casting lots was a way of leaving the choice completely to the Lord rather than human politics. Believers are called to serve wherever God places them without envy.

The east gate was given to Shelemiah, while the north gate fell to his son Zechariah. Zechariah was noted for being a wise counselor as well as a dependable guard. Practical wisdom is a great gift to bring alongside daily work in God's kingdom.

The south gate was assigned to Obed-edom, and the nearby storehouses were placed under his sons. These storehouses held sacred collections, offerings, and provisions needed for the temple workers. Guarding God's supplies is an essential trust.

The west gate and the Shallecheth gate were assigned to Shuppim and Hosah along the ascending road. The Shallecheth gate was likely where temple sweepings and ashes were carried away into the valley below. Even humble tasks like handling waste gates were handled with care and strict order.

These verses record the number of Levite guards stationed at each post each day. Six stood at the busy east gate, four at the north, four at the south, four at the storehouse, and six on the west side near the court and road. That made twenty-four daily posts in all, keeping constant watch over God's house.

This closing note summarizes that all the gatekeepers came from the clans of Korah and Merari. God set specific families over the outer safety of his dwelling place. Clear organization helps preserve peace and holiness in worship.

Other Levites were placed in charge of the temple treasuries. These rooms held both the daily provisions for sacrifices and the special gifts dedicated to God. Trustworthy keepers protected these holy goods from being wasted or stolen.

Zetham and his brother Joel, descendants of the Gershonite leader Ladan through Jehieli, were placed over the general treasuries of the Lord's house. They managed the grain, wine, oil, and money offered by the people for ongoing worship. Managing church finances honestly is a vital spiritual duty.

Among the Kohathite clans, Shebuel was appointed as chief officer over all the treasuries. Shebuel was a descendant of Moses through his son Gershom. Moses' family line held high honor and responsibility in managing the wealth of the sanctuary.

This verse traces another branch of Moses' family through his son Eliezer down to Shelomith. These family records proved that the officials in charge had the proper Levitical standing. God honors faithful family lines who serve his kingdom across generations.

Shelomith and his relatives guarded the treasuries of dedicated gifts given by King David, family heads, and army officers. A portion of the plunder won in battle was set apart specifically to repair and maintain the Lord's house. When God gives success in hard battles, he deserves the first and best of what is gained.

Shelomith also oversaw gifts dedicated over many decades by Samuel the prophet, King Saul, Abner, and Joab. All these victory spoils were gathered into one treasury for the future temple. God preserves what his people dedicate to his glory from one generation to the next.

Chenaniah and his sons from the Izharite clan were appointed to 'outside duties' across Israel as officers and judges. They served away from the sanctuary, settling disputes and teaching the law of God in local towns. God values justice and honesty in the community just as much as worship in the temple.

Hashabiah and 1,700 capable men from the Hebronite clan handled public affairs west of the Jordan River. They managed both the 'business of the Lord' and the 'service of the king,' collecting tithes and taxes while keeping the law. God is honored when public leaders serve both church and country with integrity.

Jerijah led another branch of the Hebronites, who were registered during the fortieth and final year of David's reign. Capable, strong men were found among them living at Jazer in the region of Gilead. Even at the end of his life, David remained diligent to set up godly leadership for the whole nation.

David appointed 2,700 Hebronite leaders over the eastern tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. More leaders were sent across the Jordan because those distant border tribes were farther from Jerusalem and more exposed to foreign idolatry. Wise leaders take extra care to protect the most distant and vulnerable members of God's people.
